newsitem.title: GERMANY: China Eastern sees strong ex-Germany cargo.
newsitem.headline: China Eastern sees strong ex-Germany cargo.

text.p: China Eastern Airlines said it expected strong market demand for air cargo space from Germany to China to continue for the foreseeable future.
Jie Xu, China Eastern Germany cargo sales manager, said the Shanghai-based carrier was flying at virtually 100 percent cargo load factors on its twice-weekly ex-Germany flights.
China Eastern flies Munich to Shanghai flights with a Beijing stopover with Airbus A340 aircraft with a maximum airfreight capacity of nine tonnes.
"Since last November when we added the second flight business has improved a lot. Freight comes regularly and the aircraft is always very full," he told Reuters in an interview.
"I think the market will continue to grow. Shanghai will get bigger and bigger but the other cities will grow as well," he added.

Destinations with air cargo potential included the western Chinese city of Chengdu, site of a Siemens AG power plant, Tianjing, Qingdao, Wuhan in central China and Xiamen in southern China, Xu forecast.
China Eastern, which had space for six pallets with up to 1.5 tonnes each per flight, had carried a total of 800 tonnes on its 64 flights from Germany since launching last June, Xu said.

The main air cargo goods carried were chemicals, industry machinery, electronics, with cargo generated by project business playing a key role, he added. --Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom. Tel +44 171 542 7706; Fax: 5017
